game.title: Himaneji – Idle Factory Clicker
game.description:
Himaneji is an idle factory clicker by scgf. Earn money from machines, hire workers to automate production, and choose branches in a technology tree. Rockets carry the factory loop across six stars, while rebirths award Blueprints for lasting upgrades.

Fast tapping can produce Circuit Chips for a separate upgrade tree. This beta includes daily missions and 42 achievements, with English, Japanese, and Traditional Chinese options. Saves stay in the browser; the developer provides transfer codes and an alternative official site for phones that cannot save inside itch.io.
game.how_to_play: Tap machines to earn money, buy more production capacity, and let workers automate it. Spend Circuit Chips and explore technology choices. Rebirth for permanent upgrades, then launch rockets to progress to another star.
game.controls:
Tap / click machines — earn resources
On-screen buttons — purchases, upgrades, and rockets
Menu → Transfer / Backup — create a save transfer code
game.tips:
Back up a transfer code before changing devices or clearing browser data.
Review either-or technology choices before committing.
If saving fails on a phone, follow the developer’s official-site link.
game.features:
Worker automation and away earnings
Six-star rocket progression
Blueprint rebirth upgrades
Circuit Chip upgrade tree
42 achievements and daily missions
English, Japanese, and Traditional Chinese
Browser save transfer codes
game.short_description: Tap machines, automate a factory, and launch rockets across six stars.

game.title: Sir, We Have a Situation
game.description:
Sir, We Have a Situation is an idle strategy demo by deskgeneral. Command a base against oversized everyday objects, beginning with a giant pigeon. Buildings grow as they are upgraded, and trained troops keep fighting while the tab is closed.

Six encounters bring different weaknesses, resistances, and signaled attacks. Support abilities and changing weather affect the response. The developer estimates a 45–60 minute demo ending in a debrief.
game.how_to_play: Build and upgrade the base, train troops, and inspect each target’s strengths and weaknesses. Use support when attacks are signaled, adjust for weather, and complete Command objectives through all six encounters.
game.controls:
Hover buildings — open management options
Q / W / E — call support
Use the on-screen interface for base upgrades and troop training.
game.tips:
Choose troops that suit the target: the flamingo resists mortars.
Time support around signaled attacks.
Account for reduced rifle effectiveness during fog.
game.features:
Six-target browser demo
Visible building upgrades
Automatic combat and offline progress
Target-specific weaknesses and resistances
Weather effects
Command objectives and commendations
game.short_description: Build a military base and deploy automatic troops against six absurd giant targets.

game.title: Idle Dreadnought
game.description:
Idle Dreadnought is a space shooter by Griffiths Games with automatic aiming, firing, and loot collection. Start with a Hammerhead frigate and spend alloy and EP on upgrades. The shipyard offers separate Corvette, Destroyer, and Carrier hulls with additional mounts and room slots.

Choose weapons with distinct firing arcs and advance through hostile sectors and capital-ship bosses. A challenge sector changes rules weekly. The free browser edition has no ads; the developer describes rewarded ads separately for the mobile edition.
game.how_to_play: Let the ship fight and collect alloy and EP. Fit weapons to mounts and invest in upgrades, then commission new hulls through the Berths and choose when to advance into deeper sectors.
game.controls:
Mouse / touch — interface buttons
Esc — back or close a screen
Space during combat — change speed
U during combat — upgrades
P during combat — pause
Enter in shipyard — launch
Tab / 1–5 in shipyard — switch sections
Enter / Space on run summary — continue
game.tips:
Consider each mount’s firing arc when choosing a weapon.
Review hull capacity before commissioning the next ship.
Use pause and speed controls while planning upgrades.

Automatic turret combat and loot collection
Four distinct ship hulls
Individual weapon mounts and firing arcs
Capital-ship bosses
Weekly challenge-sector rules
Mouse, touch, and keyboard support
Ad-free browser edition

game.title: Idle Island
game.description:
Idle Island is a cozy incremental prototype by Cosmos07. Gather coconuts, recruit animal helpers, and develop a tropical home with huts, sawmills, docks, and quarries. Building placement matters because nearby trees, rocks, and palms provide boosts.

Explore five zones, respond to storms and boars, fish, and collect messages from a previous captain’s journal. Progress continues while you are away. The Godot prototype supports English and Spanish through Map → Settings.
game.how_to_play: Gather resources and recruit helpers. Place production buildings near useful terrain, unlock cloud-covered areas, and respond to island events. Collect washed-up bottles to uncover the captain’s story.
game.controls:

See the original itch.io page and in-game interface for specific controls.
Map → Settings — language selection
game.tips:
Check nearby terrain before placing a production building.
Watch the fishing bobber for a bite.
Use Map → Settings to choose your language.

game.title: The Excavation Project
game.description:
The Excavation Project is a short digging game by Basilium. Begin by scraping through a small patch of ground, sell the stones you uncover, and improve your equipment to reach deeper layers and hidden gems. The official page presents excavation automation as part of the progression.

Built with Unity, the game is designed for runs of roughly 15–30 minutes. There is no save system, so a run needs to be completed in one session.
game.how_to_play: Use your current tool to dig, collect stones, and sell them. Reinvest in better tools and excavation upgrades, then work deeper into the patch of land.
game.controls:
Left mouse button — use tool
Right mouse button — rotate camera
WASD — move camera
1–7 — select tools
game.tips:
Allow time for a full run: progress cannot be saved.
Move and rotate the camera to inspect the excavation.
Use tool shortcuts when switching between tasks.

Digging and stone selling
Tool upgrades
Hidden gems
Excavation automation
Camera movement and rotation
Short 15–30 minute runs
No save system
game.short_description: Dig for valuable stones, sell your finds, and improve your excavation tools.

game.title: Lost Warden
game.description:
Lost Warden is Arknoid’s retro arcade shooter, reworked from a 2017 project. Pilot a fighter through enemy formations and build up stackable power-ups. Damage can weaken an accumulated build; movement slows while firing.

The current Godot build supports solo runs, local two-player co-op, keyboard or gamepad controls, and local high scores. Its ongoing visual rework retains some older art.
game.how_to_play: Avoid enemy fire, shoot through waves, and collect upgrades automatically. Gather plasma cells for the beam and balance sustained fire against movement speed.
game.controls:
Arrow keys / WASD / ZQSD — move
Space — fire
Left Shift — beam with plasma charge
Esc — pause
Gamepad stick / D-pad — move
South / A — fire
East / B — beam
Start / Menu — pause
game.tips:
Release fire when mobility matters.
Keep plasma for difficult formations.
Use the developer-recommended gamepad if available.
game.features:
Score-based arcade runs
Local two-player co-op
Stackable upgrades
Shield and charged beam
Keyboard and gamepad support
Local high scores
game.short_description: Survive arcade starfighter waves alone or with a local co-op partner.

game.title: The Last Line
game.description:
The Last Line is an incremental defense game by device25. Your garrison fires automatically while you hire and upgrade ten unit types, place tactical orders, and aim the marshal’s pistol. Bosses pressure the defenses, and breaches push the army back through the Outer Wall, Inner Wall, and Keep.

Fallbacks award medals for permanent bonuses. Browser saves and up to eight hours of away earnings support longer progression. The in-development build uses WebGPU where available, with a Canvas 2D fallback.
game.how_to_play: Hire troops, improve their damage, and direct orders toward threatened lanes. Use aimed pistol shots to support the garrison. Advance or lower the threat level, and fall back for permanent medal bonuses when needed.
game.controls:
1–6 / order bar — select an order
Click a lane or point — place selected order
Right-click / Esc — cancel order
Click field without an order — aimed pistol shot
Advance / Back — raise or lower threat level
game.tips:
Aim at a target’s center for the documented critical-hit bonus.
Plan purchases around the damage milestones every 25 troops of a type.
Use orders on the lanes under pressure.
Preserve browser data to retain your save.
game.features:
Ten garrison unit types
Automatic troop fire
Tactical orders and optional Auto orders
Aimed sidearm shots
Boss encounters
Three defensive lines
Permanent medal bonuses
Browser saves and capped away earnings
game.short_description: Build an automatic garrison and issue tactical orders against an endless alien swarm.

game.title: Combat Arena Pré-Alfa

Combat Arena Pré-Alfa is a tactical multiplayer FPS prototype by Thiago.dv. The developer describes team formats from 1v1 to 4v4, ranked matches, private rooms, and a training mode. Between rounds, an economy supports buying weapons and equipment.

The arsenal spans pistols, submachine guns, shotguns, rifles, and sniper rifles. Brazilian Portuguese and English are supported. This early build’s modes and balance may change as development continues.

game.title: ROTETRA
game.description:
ROTETRA is Michael Kamm’s board-spinning block puzzler, published by sharkwithlasers. Move, rotate, drop, and hold pieces while also turning the grid to juggle incoming blocks.

The in-development browser build provides rebindable keyboard and gamepad inputs. The developer lists additional modes as plans for the full game.
game.how_to_play: Position and rotate pieces, then drop them into the grid. Turn the board to change orientation and use hold to manage pieces.
game.controls:
Left / Right — move
Z / Up — rotate piece
Down — soft drop
Space — hard drop
C — hold
A / D — rotate grid
Esc / Enter — pause
Gamepad: D-pad moves/drops; South/East rotates; shoulders hold; triggers or West/North rotate grid; Start pauses.
game.tips:
Check the board before a hard drop.
Use hold to manage awkward pieces.
Rebind controls if needed; pause is fixed.
game.features:
Rotatable board
Multiple falling pieces
Hold and drop controls
Rebindable keyboard/gamepad inputs
2D pixel art
game.short_description: Stack tetrominoes while rotating the entire board and managing multiple falling pieces.

game.title: Project Chromata
game.description:
Project Chromata is GamezEternal’s minimalist sci-fi incremental game. As the Chroma Engine, produce primary colors, combine them into new resources, and convert that production into Light to restore a star chart. Constellations award permanent bonuses.

Automation supports the growing economy, while progress reveals fragments of the universe’s history. The current in-development edition covers stages 1–10 and includes a strategic combat layer.
game.how_to_play: Allocate power to color generation, unlock mixers, and develop production chains. Automate upgrades, produce Light, and restore stars to earn constellation bonuses and uncover lore.
game.controls: See the original itch.io page and in-game interface for the developer’s control notes.
game.tips:
Check production balance before expanding mixers.
Use constellation bonuses to support the next restoration goal.
Review newly unlocked automation as the economy grows.

Color mixing and production chains
Automation
Star-chart restoration
Permanent constellation bonuses
Progress-linked lore
Stages 1–10
